title: Daemon terminates and crash-loops on operation failures outside the TimeManagerError family (DST-gap ValueError, unbounded-config pydantic ValidationError, portal-echo int() ValueError, unknown YAML timezone)
description: The wrapper's entire exception boundary — runner.run_window per-operation handlers, scheduler.run_daemon's loop guard, cli.main's final guard — catches only the TimeManagerError family (plus KeyboardInterrupt at the top). Operations legitimately raise builtin exceptions outside that family: (a) SDK TimeManager._stamp raises plain ValueError when a scheduled local time falls inside a DST gap (sdk service.py:52-57, called from create_workday/create_remote_work at :257-258/:303-304); (b) int() coercions of portal-echoed values raise plain ValueError on non-numeric data (service.py:177, 354-355, 391-398 — the create-response path at :437 is isdigit-guarded, the list/get paths are not); (c) plan_for_date constructs SDK create-models from wrapper-unbounded comment/description (TaskSection config.py:94,96 has no max_length vs SDK models.py:21,64 max_length=4000), raising pydantic.ValidationError — a ValueError subclass (pydantic_core declares ValidationError(ValueError)) — at runner.py:53, which executes before the per-operation try at :55; (d) an unknown YAML timezone raises ZoneInfoNotFoundError (KeyError subclass, config.py:188 via scheduler.py:32) because AppConfig.timezone is a plain unvalidated str while the SDK validates only its own BITRIX_TIMEZONE (sdk config.py:74-77). Every such escape kills the daemon mid-window — writes already forced on at runner.py:47-48 — and under docker-compose restart: unless-stopped the process is relaunched into the same deterministic failure. Independently reproduced: all four trigger classes escape every handler while a genuine TimeManagerError subclass is contained by the same filters (agents/verify-01/artifacts/verify_harness_result.txt). Per-principal calibration: the deterministic triggers are owner-authored config (P1 = self-inflicted, fails loudly at first run); the portal variant (P4 semi-trusted response shaping) sustains a crash-loop of the owner's own single-user automation only, with no confidentiality or integrity loss and idempotent recovery — primarily an operational robustness defect that defeats two explicit error-handling controls, rated low.
root_cause: A type-family mismatch between the SDK's failure modes and every exception boundary in the wrapper: the SDK leaks plain builtin exceptions (ValueError from _stamp DST-gap rejection and unguarded int() coercions of portal echoes; pydantic ValidationError from model bounds) across its documented domain-error taxonomy (errors.py:1,11), while runner.py:57/67/71, scheduler.py:50 and cli.py:145 catch only TimeManagerError subtypes; additionally, plan_for_date (runner.py:53) runs outside the per-operation try, and the wrapper does not mirror the SDK's 4000-char bounds or validate the YAML timezone at load, so invalid inputs surface only as escaping exceptions at run time.
intended_behavior: runner.py:46 contract: 'Apply scheduled specs for every date; one failed operation never stops the rest.' scheduler.run_daemon is a daemon loop expected to survive window failures (it already has a retry_minutes path, scheduler.py:57-63), and errors.py:1 declares domain errors that do not expose raw internals; cli.main:143-150 is meant to convert failures into clean exits. None of these hold for exceptions outside the TimeManagerError family.

trace.description: Daemon dispatch; when not dry_run, run_window forces writes on (runner.py:47-48), so the window executes real create operations that can raise before completing.

YAML enters unvalidated for the failing dimensions: TaskSection.comment/description carry no max_length (config.py:94,96) and AppConfig.timezone is a plain str with no ZoneInfo check (config.py:131); a >4000-char text or unknown zone key passes load_config cleanly.

plan_for_date(config, day) executes OUTSIDE the per-operation try beginning at line 55; constructing the SDK models (config.py:208-222) against the SDK bounds (models.py:21,64 max_length=4000) raises pydantic.ValidationError, a ValueError subclass, before any handler exists.

trace.scope: _stamp, called from create_workday (:257-258) and create_remote_work (:303-304) inside the runner try
trace.description: Plain ValueError 'The requested local time does not exist in this timezone.' for DST-gap local times; int() coercions of portal echoes (:177, :354-355, :391-398) likewise raise plain ValueError — none belongs to the TimeManagerError family the handlers catch.

trace.scope: run_window per-operation handlers (:57 UncertainWriteError, :67 NotFoundError, :71 TimeManagerError)
trace.description: The filters match only the TimeManagerError family (sdk errors.py:11-75 — no ValueError or KeyError branch); ValueError/KeyError/ValidationError pass through, defeating the module contract at :46.

except TimeManagerError only, so non-family exceptions abort the loop past its retry logic; scheduler.py:55 ZoneInfo(config.timezone) is additionally outside any handler for the YAML-timezone variant reached via today_in at :32 -> config.py:188.

The process's final boundary catches only TimeManagerError (:145) and KeyboardInterrupt (:148); any other exception terminates the daemon mid-window with a traceback, and docker-compose.yml:5 restart: unless-stopped relaunches it into the same deterministic failure (crash-loop) until the config or data is fixed.

evidence.description: plan_for_date call site confirmed outside the per-operation try that starts at :55; handlers at :57/:67/:71 confirmed to catch only UncertainWriteError/NotFoundError/TimeManagerError.
Docstring contract 'one failed operation never stops the rest' — refuted for non-family exceptions.
run_daemon loop catches only TimeManagerError; :55 ZoneInfo(config.timezone) sits outside any handler.
main catches only TimeManagerError (:145) and KeyboardInterrupt (:148); everything else propagates to the interpreter.

TaskSection.comment: str with no length bound (:96 description likewise); :131 timezone: str with no validator — contrast sdk models.py:21,64 max_length=4000 and sdk config.py:74-77 which validates only the env-side BITRIX_TIMEZONE.
_stamp raises plain ValueError for DST-gap times (check at :54-56); reproduced with Europe/Berlin 2026-03-29 02:30 in the verify harness while Europe/Moscow (default) accepted the same clock time.

int(item.get(s.day_employee, 0)) on portal-echoed values without isdigit guard (also :354-355, :391-398; the create path at :437 is guarded); reproduced with a portal-shaped echo {'ufCrm46_1742341577': '12abc'}.

TimeManagerError(Exception) base with subtypes ConfigurationError/BitrixAPIError/TransportError/SchemaError/NotFoundError/ConflictError/WritesDisabledError/UncertainWriteError (:11-75) — no ValueError or KeyError branch anywhere in the hierarchy.

DayInterval.comment max_length=4000 (:21) and TimeEntryCreate.description max_length=4000 (:64) — the bounds the wrapper fails to mirror; pydantic ValidationError is a ValueError subclass per pydantic_core stubs in the project venv.
restart: unless-stopped turns the deterministic crash into a crash-loop.

Independent sandboxed stdlib reproduction (verbatim-copied except structure and _stamp): DST-gap ValueError, portal-echo int() ValueError, ValidationError at the plan_for_date site and ZoneInfoNotFoundError all escape every boundary; control SchemaError(TimeManagerError) contained; hierarchy facts re-derived.

conditions.description: TaskSection.comment/description lack the SDK's 4000-char bound and AppConfig.timezone is an unvalidated string; the deterministic variants require such config content (over-long text, DST-gap schedule with non-default BITRIX_TIMEZONE, or an unknown zone key) — all owner-authored.

The DST-gap variant additionally requires BITRIX_TIMEZONE set to a DST-observing zone (sdk config.py:53,110; default Europe/Moscow is DST-free — verified in the harness) and a scheduled start/end inside a spring-forward gap (sdk service.py:52-57).

The malformed-echo variant requires the Bitrix portal to return non-numeric employee/id fields into service.py:177/354-355/391-398 — a compromised or corrupted system-of-record that already occupies a trusted position.
DST-gap crashes occur only on the specific gap date but are then deterministic for that day's window; config-driven variants fail on every run after the offending edit.

Under restart: unless-stopped, portal-side poison data re-triggers the crash on every restart until the data or code is fixed; writes already completed before the crash remain journaled and are deduplicated on later reruns.

execution.attacker_perspective: P4 (semi-trusted portal): shape one REST echo with a non-numeric employee/id field so get_workday/_find_duplicate/_with_item raises plain ValueError; the daemon dies mid-window and the docker restart policy loops it — sustained denial of the owner's own automation, nothing more. P1 (owner/config editor): a >4000-char comment or description, a DST-gap schedule in a non-default zone, or a typo'd YAML timezone achieves the same deterministically. Practical case is self-inflicted misconfiguration: primarily an operational robustness defect rather than a cross-principal security boundary violation, which is why severity stays low despite full defeat of the error-handling controls.
payloads: YAML task with kind: workday and a comment longer than 4000 characters (config.py:94 no bound vs sdk models.py:21 max_length=4000)
YAML 'timezone: Not/AZone' (config.py:131 unvalidated str -> ZoneInfoNotFoundError at config.py:188)
schedule start '02:30' with BITRIX_TIMEZONE=Europe/Berlin evaluated on 2026-03-29 (sdk service.py:52-57)
portal echo item shaped per service.py:166 filter with employee field '12abc' reaching int() at service.py:177
instructions: Sandboxed stdlib harness (agents/verify-01/artifacts/verify_harness_result.txt) copies the exact except structure of runner.py:52-76, scheduler.py:47-52, cli.py:143-150 with verbatim _stamp (service.py:51-58) and the verbatim int() condition (service.py:175-178); run under sandbox-exec with env -i, ulimit -t 60 -f 2048; no target package imported, dummy data only.
Each trigger is driven through the copied filters; a control SchemaError (TimeManagerError family) is driven through the same filters.
execution.observed_result: All four triggers — DST-gap ValueError (Europe/Berlin 2026-03-29 02:30; Europe/Moscow default accepted the same time), int() ValueError on a portal-shaped malformed echo, ValidationError(ValueError) at the plan_for_date call site, and ZoneInfoNotFoundError for an unknown YAML timezone — escaped every handler and reached the process top level, while the control case SchemaError(TimeManagerError) was contained by the same filters. Hierarchy facts confirmed from source: TimeManagerError has no ValueError/KeyError branch (errors.py:11-75), ZoneInfoNotFoundError is a KeyError subclass, pydantic_core declares ValidationError(ValueError).

remediation.strategy: Close the boundary mismatch at three layers: (1) make the daemon loop survivable for any Exception so a poison operation degrades to the existing retry_minutes path (SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt derive from BaseException and still propagate, preserving clean shutdown); (2) mirror the SDK's 4000-char bounds in TaskSection so over-long config fails at load_config time, where ValueError is already converted to ConfigurationError and handled cleanly; (3) validate the YAML timezone with ZoneInfo at config load. Optionally broaden the per-operation handlers in runner.py to except Exception to fully honor the :46 contract.

likelihood.reason: Every deterministic trigger is owner-authored config that fails loudly on the first run after the change (long comment, unknown zone key, DST-gap schedule requiring a non-default BITRIX_TIMEZONE — the default Europe/Moscow is DST-free, verified in the harness); the only external trigger requires a compromised or corrupted portal that already occupies a trusted position.

impact.reason: Blast radius is the owner's own single-user automation availability: the daemon dies mid-window, completed writes stand and remaining operations are skipped until restart; recovery is duplication-free via xmlId dedup and journal.reserve; no webhook secret or other confidential data appears in any of the escaping exception texts, no integrity or confidentiality loss, no privilege change.

confidence.reason: Every cited line matches the current source in both trees; the type-family mismatch is proven from sdk errors.py:11-75, the installed pydantic_core stubs and stdlib ZoneInfoNotFoundError; the escape was independently reproduced with verbatim-copied decisive logic in a sandboxed stdlib harness, including a contained control case proving the handlers work for their designed family. Severity calibrated by per-principal analysis (P1 owner self-misconfig, P4 semi-trusted portal limited to self-DoS) to low.

title: Claimed httpcore child-logger bypass leaks webhook token to stdout under -v — sink does not exist in installed httpcore 1.0.9
description: The candidate claims that with -v (DEBUG on stdout), httpcore's httpcore.http11 Trace records render request=<Request ... target=b'/rest/1/<token>/<method>.json'> on an unfiltered child logger, disclosing the full webhook token. Independent source verification of the installed stack (httpx 0.28.1, httpcore 1.0.9, h11 0.16 in A/.venv) and a verbatim stdlib harness refute the sink: httpcore's Request.__repr__ is '<Request [b'POST']>' (method only, never url/target), Trace info dicts never contain a URL object, connection traces carry host/port only, and h11 emits no logs at all. The only log record in the entire stack containing the full URL is httpx's INFO line emitted on the 'httpx' logger — the exact logger the SDK filter is installed on — and it is redacted to /rest/1/***/. The true residue is only a defense-in-depth observation: parent-logger filters indeed do not apply to child-logger records (Python logging semantics, demonstrated with a synthetic message), but no httpcore 1.0.9 child-logger record contains the token, so there is nothing to bypass.
claimed_root_cause: SDK installs _WebhookLogFilter only on loggers 'httpx' and 'httpcore' while httpcore emits through child loggers (httpcore.http11 etc.) whose records never pass the parent filter, and httpcore Trace debug records allegedly include a Request repr containing the URL target with the webhook token.

trace.description: Filter install loop confirmed verbatim: for name in ('httpx','httpcore'): getLogger(name).addFilter(_WebhookLogFilter()) — premise of the claim is accurate.
Confirmed: -v sets basicConfig(level=DEBUG, stream=sys.stdout) on every subcommand incl. daemon; root handler has no filters.

Child loggers confirmed in installed httpcore 1.0.9: 'httpcore.http11' (also connection.py 'httpcore.connection', http2, http_proxy 'httpcore.proxy', socks_proxy 'httpcore.socks'). Python logging semantics confirmed: records emitted on a child logger bypass ancestor-logger filters (only ancestor handlers run).

REFUTED SINK: actual Request.__repr__ (362-363) is f"<{cls} [{method!r}]>" -> '<Request [b'POST']>' — contains only the method, never scheme/host/target. The candidate's citation '_models.py:309-313' is URL.__repr__, and no Trace info dict ever contains a URL object.

Trace builds messages as name + key=value!r over info dicts; verified info dicts across _async/http11.py:80-105 (request object), _async/connection.py:117-124 (host/port/local_address/timeout/socket_options) and 153-161 (ssl_context/server_hostname/timeout) plus return values — none renders the URL or token. Only url-bearing strings in httpcore are RuntimeError texts using request.url.origin (host, no path/token).

The only record containing the full URL is logger.info('HTTP Request: %s %s ...', request.url, ...) on the single 'httpx' logger (_client.py:117) — the same logger object the SDK filter is installed on; the record is redacted to /rest/1/***/ (confirmed in the verify harness and in the hunter's own artifact line 2).

evidence.description: Own sandboxed verbatim harness (filter, redact, install loop, _trace.py formatting, Request.__repr__, httpx INFO format copied verbatim; dummy token): 'faithful httpcore.http11 trace lines contain raw token: False'; 'request=<Request [b'POST']>: True'; 'httpx INFO line redacted to /rest/1/***/: True'; the raw token appears only in the clearly-marked synthetic semantics-probe line that no httpcore code emits.
Installed httpcore 1.0.9: Request.__repr__ renders only the HTTP method. Lines 309-313 are URL.__repr__ (class name 'URL', str scheme), which the hunter mis-cited as Request.__repr__.
h11 0.16.0 contains no logging usage at all (grep over h11 package -> no files); httpx uses exactly one logger 'httpx' (_client.py:117).

Hunter's 'raw token' lines used the fabricated format request=Request(scheme=b'https', host=..., target=b'/rest/1/TESTTOKEN123/...') — matches neither Request.__repr__ nor URL.__repr__ of httpcore 1.0.9 and is produced by no httpcore code path; their 'bypass = True' verdict is an artifact of that fabrication.
Dependency constraint httpx>=0.28,<0.29 with installed httpx 0.28.1 + httpcore 1.0.9 fixes the audited stack; no version in this range renders the target in Request.__repr__ traces.

reason: Core premise true but sink refuted: the filter is installed only on parent loggers 'httpx'/'httpcore' and parent filters indeed never apply to child-logger records — however, with the installed httpx 0.28.1/httpcore 1.0.9, no child-logger record ever contains the webhook token. httpcore's Request.__repr__ renders only the HTTP method; Trace info dicts carry the Request object, host/port/TLS kwargs, or return values, never the URL; h11 does not log. The single URL-bearing record (httpx INFO) is on the filtered 'httpx' logger and is redacted to /rest/1/***/, confirmed by independent verbatim reproduction and by the hunter's own artifact. The claimed impact (full token on stdout under -v, docker logs/cron disclosure) is therefore not realizable via the described path; the hunter's demonstrating harness emitted a message format that no httpcore 1.0.9 code produces. Remaining observation — logger-level redaction is not defense-in-depth against child loggers — is a hardening suggestion (extend filter to httpcore.* children or redact at handler level), not a vulnerability, and does not meet even informational severity as a token-disclosure finding. Per the severity-≤-demonstrated-impact rule the candidate cannot stand as medium.

title: Неограниченное разбиение на страницы в list_items: постоянно увеличивающиеся различные курсоры + limit=None приводят к вечному циклу и неограниченной памяти
description: BitrixClient.list_items завершает работу только при достижении запрошенного limit, отсутствии 'next' или ТОЧНОМ повторении курсора (set-membership для значений start). Злонамеренный/скомпрометированный портал, возвращающий валидные страницы 200-OK с постоянно увеличивающимися различными next-курсорами, заставляет цикл работать вечно, в то время как список items (и seen-set) растет без границ. Таймауты на каждый запрос не срабатывают, так как каждый HTTP-запрос успешно завершается. Три места вызова передают limit=None (пути list_time_entries, list_remote_work и _find_duplicate overlap в SDK service.py), которые используются плановыми записями и чтениями в A; демон A не имеет внешнего asyncio-таймаута, поэтому одно зависшее чтение навсегда останавливает все будущие запланированные прогоны без ошибок или логов.
root_cause: Обнаружение плохого курсора в client.py:123-125 проверяет только точное повторение значения start; оно не ограничивает количество страниц или общее количество элементов. В комбинации со сторонами вызова, передающими limit=None (по умолчанию), неограниченная последовательность курсоров никогда не завершает цикл. Пер-запросный HTTP-таймаут (client.py:30) не может ограничить цикл, потому что каждый запрос завершается успешно.
intended_behavior: Строка документации client.py:116: 'Читать страницы списка до исчерпания или запрошенного limit, обнаруживая плохие курсоры.' Исчерпание должно быть ограничено; неограниченная последовательность курсоров сама по себе является плохим курсором и должна быть обнаружена, а не потребляться вечно.

trace.description: Цикл while True начинается с start=0; seen set инициализируется пустым; limit по умолчанию равен None от неограниченных вызывающих сторон.

start = int(body['next']): злоумышленник контролирует курсор через тело ответа портала; строго возрастающая последовательность никогда не повторяет членство в seen (:123-125), поэтому защита от повторения никогда не срабатывает.
Вызывает list_items без limit (по умолчанию None); достижимо из runner.py:83 (путь on_existing_entries=skip) и runner.py:128 (show_day), а также из _find_duplicate:340 для элементов времени.
Вызывает list_items без limit; используется runner.py:120 (show_day) и _find_duplicate:353 (дедупликация удаленной работы перед каждой запланированной записью удаленной работы).
Вызывает list_items на remote_type без limit; выполняется внутри _finish для каждой операции create_remote_work — т.е. на запланированном пути записи.

summary = await _run_once(...) без asyncio.timeout/wait_for; grep обоих src-деревьев не находит никакого внешнего обработчика таймаута, поэтому одно зависание list_items блокирует демона навсегда (никаких срабатываний повторной попытки, так как зависание не является TimeManagerError).
items.extend(page) на каждой итерации без общего ограничения; цикл никогда не выходит, так как 'next' всегда присутствует, а limit равен None — корутинка зависает навсегда с монотонным ростом памяти.

evidence.description: Условия завершения перечислены в source: проверка limit<1 (:117-118), точное повторение курсора (:123-125), срез limit (:141-142), отсутствие 'next' (:143-144), невалидный int курсор (:145-148). Нет ограничения на количество страниц/элементов.
timeout=settings.timeout применяется через httpx.AsyncClient — это строго пер-запросный таймаут; запросы с 200-OK завершаются успешно, поэтому он не может ограничить цикл.

Исчерпывающий grep по обоим репозиториям: ровно 6 мест вызова list_items; :196-210 (list_time_entries), :217-235 (list_remote_work) и :344-351 (overlap scan) не передают limit; :164-169 и :322-324 передают limit=2, :241-243 ограничивает limit 1..100.
run_daemon while True цикл без внешнего таймаута для _run_once; только TimeManagerError попадает в retry_minutes — вечное ожидание никогда не прерывается и не регистрируется в логе.

Независимое воспроизведение с дословно скопированным циклом (подтверждено diff после удаления await и дедента) под sandbox-exec: 'malicious-distinct -> NO TERMINATION: HARNESS ABORT: exceeded 5000 pages; portal_calls=5001'; повторный курсор контроля -> SchemaError после 2 вызовов; limit=2 -> 2 элемента после 1 страницы; корректное исчерпание -> возвращается. Совпадает с hunter артефактом h4_pagination.out.txt.

conditions.description: Конечная точка Bitrix24, на которую указывает URL вебхука, должна быть злонамеренной, скомпрометированной или грубо некорректной и возвращать синтаксически валидные страницы 200-OK, чей 'next' курсор строго увеличивается всегда — проходя каждую проверку схемы, при этом каждый запрос успешно завершается.

Уязвимый путь должен быть выполнен с limit=None (три места по умолчанию для чтения/дедупликации) и без внешнего супервизора процесса (например, перезапуска Docker с ограничениями памяти), чтобы превратить вечное ожидание в постоянный простой демона и/или OOM.

execution.attacker_perspective: Измененный портал контролирует тело каждого ответа crm.item.list. Вместо того чтобы портить данные или возвращать ошибки, он держит владельца занятым: каждый ответ содержит пару валидных словарей элементов и next = start + page_size, так что клиент вежливо запрашивает следующую страницу всегда. Все проверки схемы проходят, каждый HTTP-запрос успешно завершается, и клиент никогда не возвращается — запланированный демон владельца молча перестает применять какие-либо будущие записи, в то время как память тратится на отброшенные страницы.
payloads: Тело ответа заглушки на каждый запрос: {'result': {'items': [{'id': start+i, 'title': 'stub'} для i в range(2)]}, 'next': start + 2} — валидные элементы, всегда присутствует 'next', монотонно возрастающие различные целочисленные курсоры. Контроль повторения курсора: то же самое с 'next': 50 всегда.
instructions: Скопирован дословно цикл из client.py:117-148 (единственный await удален; блок diff-проверен идентичным исходному после дедента) в класс с порталом-заглушкой; запуск через sandbox-exec (deny network*, deny file-write* кроме scratch) с ulimit -t 60 -f 2048, /usr/bin/python3. Кейс 1: заглушка постоянно увеличивающихся курсоров, limit=None. Кейс 2 (контроль): повторяющийся курсор. Кейс 3 (контроль): limit=2 на злонамеренной заглушке. Кейс 4 (контроль): честное исчерпание без 'next'.
execution.observed_result: malicious-distinct + limit=None: NO TERMINATION, тест прерван на 5000 страниц / 10000 элементов / 5001 вызов портала — цикл никогда бы не вышел. repeated-cursor контроль: SchemaError 'Bitrix repeated the page cursor.' после 2 вызовов портала (существующая защита работает). limit=2 контроль: вернулось ровно 2 элемента после 1 страницы (ограничение работает). honest-exhausted контроль: вернулось нормально после 1 страницы. Результаты идентичны hunter h4_pagination.out.txt.

remediation.strategy: Ограничить общее количество элементов (страниц) в самом цикле, чтобы неограниченное поведение курсора стало обнаруживаемой ошибкой, а не зависанием. Ограничение должно быть на уровне модуля, превышать любой легитимный результат с фильтром по владельцу (например, 10 000) и вызывать SchemaError, соответствующую контракту 'обнаружения плохих курсоров'. title: Unscoped .env loading in Settings.from_env installs arbitrary env keys (SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR, HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY, BITRIX_STATE_PATH) that later steer httpx TLS trust, proxy routing, and the journal path

title: Kind-blind wrapper idempotency key makes WorkdayCreate and RemoteWorkCreate collide, permanently and silently suppressing the remote operation
description: The wrapper's idempotency_key (A config.py:227-234) hashes only json.dumps(spec.model_dump(mode='json'), sort_keys=True). WorkdayCreate and RemoteWorkCreate are empty subclasses of DayInterval (B models.py:39-44) with identical field sets (day/start/end/comment), so specs with equal values serialize byte-identically and yield the SAME key (independently reproduced: auto:2026-10-21:ae6e75a5 for both). KIND_ORDER (config.py:30) applies workday first; its create binds the scoped journal key sha256(portal:user:key) (service.py:417-420) to the workday operation_id. The remote create derives the same scoped key for a different operation_id (kind is in the SDK operation identity, service.py:85-91), so journal.bind_key raises ConflictError (journal.py:58-59) before the duplicate short-circuit at service.py:421 — even when a matching remote record already exists. ConflictError is a TimeManagerError (errors.py:52-55), caught by runner.py:71-75 as warning + skipped++; RunSummary.ok ignores skipped (runner.py:34-36), so the scheduler exits 0 and never retries (scheduler.py:54-57). The request_keys binding has no cleanup path anywhere in journal.py, so the scheduled remote record is suppressed on every run, indefinitely, while preview (dry_run returns at service.py:415-416 before bind_key) still shows both operations as planned. Severity is downgraded from the proposal's medium: the product's own docs mark kind: workday as 'do not use' (docs/setup.md:260-265 — the portal webhook gets ACCESS_DENIED on workday add; the day comes from SKUD marks or remote robots), the shipped example YAML contains no workday task at all, and triggering additionally requires byte-identical start/end/comment on the same weekday — a semantically contradictory pairing. The defect is real and structural, but its reachability is low-likelihood misconfiguration, not a natural one.
root_cause: The wrapper key payload lacks a kind/type discriminator while the SDK journal contract binds one scoped idempotency key to exactly one immutable logical operation (journal.py:53-61). Two different logical operations (workday create vs remote create) can therefore derive one key, and the first-bound operation permanently owns it; there is no release path for request_keys.
intended_behavior: Stable per-date, per-kind, per-parameters key so reruns never duplicate records (config.py:228 docstring) — different operation kinds must never share a key, and every scheduled spec must receive a write attempt or a visible failure that affects run status.

Scope and journal key are sha256(portal_url:user_id:idempotency_key) (lines 417-419) — identical for both kinds since only the wrapper key string feeds it.

RunSummary.ok (runner.py:34-36) checks only failed and uncertain; scheduler.py:54,57 exits 0 and skips retry, so the daemon reports success while the remote record is never created, on every run.

WorkdayCreate(DayInterval) and RemoteWorkCreate(DayInterval) (lines 39-44) are empty subclasses — identical field sets day/start/end/comment; sort_keys makes declaration order irrelevant, so dumps are byte-identical for equal values. TimeEntryCreate (lines 59-82) has disjoint fields and cannot collide.

Independent sandbox reproduction: payload workday == payload remote; idempotency_key(workday) == idempotency_key(remote) == auto:2026-10-21:ae6e75a5; entry key differs; scoped journal key identical for both ops; bind_key(workday op): ok; bind_key(remote op): ConflictError; control rebind same op: ok; request_keys row persists bound to the workday operation.

Shipped example pairs NO workday+remote tasks: only remote (fri) and time_entry (mon-fri). Header explicitly states the workday is NOT created by this tool — the example config itself would NOT trigger the collision.

This contradicts the product's documented usage: docs/setup.md:260-265 marks kind: workday as 'do not use' and the shipped example YAML has no workday task. Scheduling a manual office workday and remote work for the same date is also semantically contradictory, which further narrows realistic reachability.

The journal request_keys row for the scoped key must exist, bound to the workday operation_id — it is created by the first apply of the workday op (even if the subsequent crm.item.add fails, e.g. ACCESS_DENIED, since bind_key at service.py:420 precedes the write at service.py:434) and there is no cleanup path in journal.py, so the condition persists indefinitely.

execution.attacker_perspective: Not attacker-driven. A config author pairs a kind: workday task with a kind: remote task for the same weekday with identical parameters (e.g. both 09:00-18:00 with empty comments). The tool then silently drops every scheduled remote-work record for those dates while reporting success.

Place both tasks in config/*.yaml, run 'bitrix-auto preview --date D' (both ops shown as planned — dry_run returns before bind_key), then 'bitrix-auto apply --date D': the workday op binds the scoped key; every run of the remote op thereafter raises ConflictError inside bind_key, logged as warning, counted skipped, run still exits 0.
execution.observed_result: Sandbox harness: payload workday == payload remote; idempotency_key(workday) == idempotency_key(remote) == auto:2026-10-21:ae6e75a5; idempotency_key(entry) differs; SDK operation ids differ (kind in identity); scoped journal key identical for both ops; bind_key(workday op): ok; bind_key(remote op): ConflictError 'This Idempotency-Key has already been used with different parameters.'; control rebind same op: ok; request_keys holds exactly one row bound to the workday operation. Matches the hunter artifact h1_key_collision.out.txt, derived independently.

remediation.strategy: Add the spec kind to the hashed payload in the wrapper's idempotency_key so different operation kinds can never share a key. Keys change once; already-created records remain reconcilable through the SDK operation_id/xmlId path (duplicate detection does not depend on the wrapper key), so no journal migration is needed. Optionally make RunSummary.ok account for skipped-with-error, or at minimum emit a distinct log level, so permanent suppressions are visible; and/or have the wrapper reject kind: workday configs outright while it is documented as unusable on this portal.

code_changes.fixed_code:
def idempotency_key(spec: WorkdayCreate | RemoteWorkCreate | TimeEntryCreate) -> str:
    """Stable per-date, per-kind, per-parameters key so reruns never duplicate records."""
    import hashlib
    import json

    payload = json.dumps(
        {"kind": type(spec).__name__, "spec": spec.model_dump(mode="json")},
        sort_keys=True,
        ensure_ascii=False,
    )
    digest = hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
    return f"auto:{spec.day.isoformat()}:{digest}"

The candidate's 'natural configuration' claim is refuted by these repo-internal controls; only an operator who ignores the documentation reaches the bug.

impact.reason: If triggered, the suppression is silent and permanent: the scheduled remote-work record is never created, the run exits 0 with no retry, only a single warning line per operation is logged, preview keeps showing the operation as planned (preview/apply parity violation), the request_keys binding never expires, and dependent time entries for those dates cascade into skipped NotFoundError until robots create a day some other way. No confidentiality, authentication or privilege impact; harm is integrity/availability of the tool's own scheduled records.

confidence.reason: Every link was read in current source (models, key function, ordering, journal SQL, service._finish ordering, error hierarchy, runner/scheduler semantics) and the full chain was reproduced with an independent verbatim-copy harness under sandbox-exec; the only judgment call is severity, downgraded from the proposal because the repo's own example and docs establish that the triggering configuration is documented-unsupported rather than natural.

title: Compose service runs as container root (no USER/user:) with rw ./state bind: umask-driven 0644 journal becomes root-owned on the host — operator lockout from own state and host-mode --once breakage; world-readability leg overlaps the already-filed journal-0644 root cause

title: Wrapper .gitignore ignores compose-only state/ but not .state/ — the documented host/cron journal default, so one git add -A publishes the personal work-activity SQLite
description: The wrapper repo's .gitignore lists state/ (the Docker-compose host volume dir) but has no .state/ entry, while the SDK's paired .gitignore does ignore .state/. The SDK's default journal path is CWD-relative .state/operations.sqlite3 (BITRIX_STATE_PATH unset); the wrapper sets that variable only in docker-compose.yml and omits it from .env.example. The documented host/cron flow (README.md:54-68) runs apply/daemon from the repo root, so the first write-mode run creates <repo>/.state/operations.sqlite3 (unignored: git check-ignore exit 1). README misdirects the operator by documenting the journal at state/operations.sqlite3 (the ignored Docker path) and AGENTS.md's Never-list names state/ but not .state/. The journal stores work-activity plaintext (day/time/remote comments and descriptions), the portal origin via item_url, USER_ID via assignedById, and item/workday IDs — exactly the value classes the repo's own Boundaries forbid committing. No pre-commit hook, secret scanner, or CI exists to catch it. A single git add -A + push to the public-prepared GitHub remote publishes the personal database.
root_cause: Path-coverage mismatch between two paired repos and two execution modes: the SDK default (CWD-relative .state/, sdk .gitignore:5) was never mirrored into the wrapper .gitignore, which instead covers only the compose-pinned state/ path; the wrapper additionally never documents or overrides BITRIX_STATE_PATH for host/cron mode, leaving the default active and uncovered.
intended_behavior: All local runtime state produced by any documented execution mode (Docker or host/cron) must be excluded from version control, consistent with the repo's own Boundaries forbidding real portal data (домен, USER_ID, ID дней и карточек, названия задач) in commits; the journal location should be either ignored (.state/ in .gitignore) or defaulted under the already-ignored state/ directory, and documented accurately.

title: Ошибки открытия журнала (sqlite3) обходят контракт санитизированных ошибок: сырой traceback и код 1 в обоих CLI
description: Операции открытия/инициализации SQLite-журнала в OperationJournal конвертируются в ConflictError только частично. sqlite3.connect (journal.py:28) выполняется до начала try (строка 30), а единственный обработчик (строка 44) ловит лишь sqlite3.OperationalError. Два независимых пути обходят обработник и оба CLI: (a) повреждённый/мусорный файл журнала -> executescript возбуждает sqlite3.DatabaseError ('file is not a database'), который является РОДИТЕЛЕМ OperationalError, а не его подклассом, и потому не перехватывается; (b) если BITRIX_STATE_PATH указывает на каталог, connect возбуждает sqlite3.OperationalError до входа в try. Ни sdk cli.py:122 (кортеж TimeManagerError/ValidationError/ValueError/OSError), ни A cli.py:145 (только TimeManagerError) не ловит sqlite3.Error; per-op обработчики A runner.py:57/67/71 и цикл демона scheduler.py:41 также ловят только подклассы TimeManagerError. Оба CLI не имеют запасного перехвата sqlite3.Error.
intended_behavior: Любая ошибка журнала должна превращаться в доменную ConflictError ('The operation journal is busy or unavailable. title: Daemon stdout logs persist work-activity metadata (dates, record kinds, item IDs, real portal domain in item_url) into policy-free deployment sinks: Docker default json-file and cron mail spool
description: Re-derived from current source and independently reproduced via a verbatim sandbox render (agents/verify-14/artifacts/stdout_render.txt, byte-shape identical to the hunter artifact): the CLI configures INFO logging to sys.stdout (cli.py:137-142) and the daemon — the default container workload per Dockerfile:13-14 — emits per-record lines 'YYYY-MM-DD <Kind>: <status> (item_id=N, url=<portal>/page/timemenedzher/.../details/N/)' (runner.py:111), window/summary/retry lines (scheduler.py:33-35,61-62), date+count skip lines (runner.py:85-89) and error lines (runner.py:58-74) whose only redaction, redact() at sdk errors.py:6-8, masks the /rest/<uid>/<secret> webhook segment alone — portal origin, item IDs and dates survive (proven in agents/verify-14/artifacts/redact_scope.txt). No free-text YAML comment/description ever enters a daemon line (SDK warnings are fixed strings), and wrapper src contains zero logger.debug calls. The repo sets no retention or access policy for this stdout copy: docker-compose.yml has no logging: section so the documented Docker default (json-file, unbounded absent daemon-level rotation) applies — a deployment fact treated as blocker material, not probed; README.md:43 instructs reading via docker compose logs; README.md:63-68 documents a cron mode with no output-redirection or MAILTO guidance, defaulting stdout to the local mail spool. AGENTS.md's Never-list (portal domain/IDs never publishable) formally targets published artifacts, and architecture.md:40's retention TODO covers only the SQLite journal — nothing covers stdout. Whether any unauthorized principal can actually read these sinks, and whether retention is truly unbounded on the deployment host, is not source-derivable, so the consequence side requires owner validation even though the emission itself is fully source-settled.
claimed_root_cause: The wrapper logs operation results at INFO to stdout with no work-data redaction (redact() covers webhook tokens only) and no retention policy anywhere in the repo, while shipping the daemon as a container whose compose file declares no logging: policy and documenting a cron invocation without redirection or MAILTO — so work-activity metadata including the real portal domain lands in whatever default, policy-free sink the deployment host provides (Docker json-file under /var/lib/docker, readable by any docker-group member via docker logs; or the cron mail spool), surviving deletion of state/ and config/.

trace.description: logging.basicConfig(level=INFO, stream=sys.stdout) applies to every command including daemon; all daemon output goes to stdout, not stderr, with no filter separating work-data-bearing lines.

logger.info("%s: %s (item_id=%s, url=%s)", label, result.status, result.item_id, result.item_url) where label = f"{day.isoformat()} {type(spec).__name__}" (runner.py:99) — emits date, record kind, status, portal item ID and full portal URL per operation.

_url() builds item_url = f"{portal_url}/page/timemenedzher/{section}/type/{entity_type_id}/details/{item_id}/"; attached to every OperationResult at service.py:397 and returned to the wrapper, which logs it verbatim.
portal_url property returns the scheme://netloc of the real production webhook URL — the true portal origin, embedded unredacted in every logged item_url.
Window line 'Running window D1..D2 (dry_run=...)' and 'Summary: created=... existing=...' emit the full processed date window and outcome counts daily; scheduler.py:61-62 adds retry/next-run lines.

Error paths log label+error text (UncertainWriteError with operation_id hash, NotFoundError with dates, TimeManagerError/BitrixAPIError); the only redaction applied is sdk redact() which masks the /rest/<uid>/<secret> segment and nothing else (errors.py:6-8) — portal domain and item URLs survive.
ENTRYPOINT python -m bitrix_auto_manage + CMD daemon — the container's default workload is the daemon, so its stdout feeds the container log driver on every deployment.

Entire 16-line file declares no logging: section — no driver, no rotation/retention options; the documented Docker default (json-file, unbounded) applies unless the host overrides it, a deployment fact.

Documented cron mode ('bitrix-auto daemon --once', crontab '5 18 * * *') gives no output-redirection or MAILTO guidance, so cron's default behavior mails the daemon's stdout to the local mail spool; README.md:43 likewise instructs 'docker compose logs -f' for the compose mode, where the json-file copy accumulates.

evidence.description: basicConfig(level=INFO, stream=sys.stdout) — confirmed in current source.
Per-record emission of date+kind, status, item_id, item_url; grep of wrapper src shows the complete call set with zero logger.debug calls.
_url construction verified; item_url attached at service.py:397.
portal_url = scheme://netloc of the real webhook — real portal origin in every logged URL.
redact() regex masks only the webhook secret segment; sandbox render (agents/verify-14/artifacts/redact_scope.txt) shows portal domain and item_url pass through untouched.

Independent verbatim render under sandbox-exec reproduces every daemon line shape byte-identically to the hunter artifact, including '2026-10-23 RemoteWorkCreate: created (item_id=4242, url=https://portal.example.org/page/timemenedzher/udalennaya_rabota/type/1052/details/4242/)' with dummy domain only.
ENTRYPOINT/CMD make daemon the default container workload.
Full 16-line file: no logging: section — no driver or rotation policy in repo.
'docker compose logs -f' documented as the way to watch run logs.
cron/Task-Scheduler mode documented without redirection or MAILTO guidance.
Retention TODO covers only the SQLite journal ('Ретеншн журнала приложением не ограничен') — nothing covers stdout; AGENTS.md Never-list formally targets published artifacts, not host-local logs.

blockers: Effective Docker log driver and rotation are a host fact: docker-compose.yml declares no logging: section, but the deployment host's daemon.json may override the documented json-file default (e.g. local driver with rotation); unbounded retention of the sink cannot be confirmed or refuted from source, and docker probing is out of scope for this audit.

Readership of the json-file sink is a host fact: file permissions under /var/lib/docker/containers/*/*-json.log and docker-group membership (any member can read the logs via docker logs without host-file access) are not derivable from source.

Whether the cron path is actually used, its MAILTO setting, and the existence and permissions of the local mail spool (/var/mail/*) are deployment facts; README only suggests '5 18 * * *' without redirection guidance.
Actual deployment mode (docker compose vs cron vs manual runs) is not recorded anywhere in the repo, so which sink even applies is unknown.

Existence of any lower-trust principal on this single-user-by-design personal-automation host is unknown; without one, the unauthorized-reader consequence reduces to owner/root-only access and the finding downgrades to hygiene.

validation_plan.local: Source-side checks (already performed, no deployment needed): full read of docker-compose.yml confirms no logging: block; grep confirms zero logger.debug in wrapper src and that no free-text YAML comment/description enters any daemon line (SDK warnings are fixed strings); verbatim sandbox render at agents/verify-14/artifacts/stdout_render.txt reproduces every emitted line shape and redact_scope.txt proves redact() masks only the webhook secret segment.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed checks only: (1) docker inspect bitrix-auto-manage --format '{{.HostConfig.LogConfig}}' to record the effective driver and opts; (2) sudo ls -l /var/lib/docker/containers/*/*-json.log to record sink permissions, size and whether rotation is active; (3) from a non-owner docker-group account (if any exists), run docker logs bitrix-auto-manage and check whether item_url lines expose the real portal domain and item IDs; (4) crontab -l to check MAILTO and whether a 'bitrix-auto daemon --once' entry exists; (5) ls -l /var/mail/* to check for a cron mail spool holding daemon stdout; plus record whether any non-owner user accounts exist on the host.

title: Unfinished remote-work interval started before the target day bypasses the conflict scan, creating overlapping records
description: _find_duplicate's remote-work conflict set is the union of two queries. (a) The overlap predicate (service.py:344-351) requires existing.remote_end > plan_start ('>remote_end' filter), which a record with unset remote_end can never satisfy; (b) the unfinished-interval catch same_day = list_remote_work(spec.day) (service.py:353) bounds remote_start to the target local day via '>=remote_start day 00:00' / '<remote_start next day 00:00' (service.py:219-223), so a record started on a previous day is excluded. An unfinished interval started before the target day appears in NEITHER result, by_id is empty, the conflict loop (service.py:356-361) never runs, and None is returned; _finish then proceeds to journal.reserve + crm.item.add (service.py:427,434), writing an overlapping remote-work record to the production portal as the webhook owner. No portal compromise is needed: a stale unfinished remote interval left from normal UI usage suffices, and every subsequent scheduled day then creates one more overlap. This defeats the explicit unfinished-interval conflict control stated in the code comment at service.py:352 and asserted in the SDK's own integration test. Independently reproduced with a verbatim harness from current source (agents/verify-03/artifacts/verify_overlap.out.txt): cases A (end=None) and A2 (end='') both return None and reach crm.item.add, while controls behave as intended (unfinished same-day -> ConflictError; finished cross-day overlap -> ConflictError; back-to-back -> allowed).
root_cause: The remote-work conflict scan has a two-query design with a coverage gap: the overlap predicate cannot match records with an unset remote_end (empty/NULL datetime never satisfies the '>' range comparison), and the dedicated unfinished-interval query list_remote_work(spec.day) only covers remote_start values within the target day. An unfinished record with remote_start strictly before the target day falls into the gap between the two queries, so the union by_id is empty and the ConflictError branch at service.py:359-360 is unreachable for it.
intended_behavior: service.py:352 comment 'An unfinished manual remote interval on the same day is also a conflict' and tests/integration/test_service.py:421-440 (test_manual_remote_duplicate_and_unfinished_interval): when an existing manual remote record's remote_end is set to None, create_remote_work must raise ConflictError and no crm.item.add may fire. Intent: any unfinished remote interval overlapping the plan (regardless of which day it started on) blocks the write, because an open-ended interval logically extends into the plan window.

trace.description: The daemon applies each scheduled day's RemoteWorkCreate directly through the SDK; repo A performs no overlap pre-scan of its own (its only list_remote_work use is the read-only show_day at runner.py:120), so the SDK conflict scan is the sole control.
Public write entry: builds fields (remote_start/remote_end from the plan), then delegates to _finish with no additional scanning.

Exact-duplicate query by xmlId+assignedById cannot catch the unfinished record: a manually created record has no btm_<hash> xmlId, and a tool-created record from a different day/spec has a different operation_id (identity hash covers the full spec, service.py:85-91), so 'ours' is empty and this path returns nothing.

Overlap predicate sends filters {'<remote_start': plan_end, '>remote_end': plan_start}; the unfinished record satisfies '<remote_start' (yesterday 20:00 < today 18:00) but its unset remote_end cannot satisfy '>remote_end', so the server excludes it.
The unfinished-interval catch queries only records with remote_start in [target day 00:00, next day 00:00) (filters at service.py:219-223), so a record started on a previous day is not returned.
by_id = union of overlapping + same_day is empty, the loop never iterates, the ConflictError at :359-360 is unreachable, and _find_duplicate returns None.

duplicate=None passes the gate at :421; journal.reserve (:427) runs and crm.item.add (:434) creates a new remote-work record overlapping the still-open interval from the previous day. The post-create verification read (:456-466) only emits warnings and never re-checks overlaps.

evidence.description: Verbatim overlap filter: f"<{s.remote_start}": plan.fields[s.remote_end], f">{s.remote_end}": plan.fields[s.remote_start] — second clause demands a non-empty remote_end on the existing record.

Comment 'An unfinished manual remote interval on the same day is also a conflict.' — the author's own statement that unfinished intervals are conflicts, with the mitigation deliberately scoped to the same day only; the word 'also' confirms the overlap predicate alone cannot catch unfinished records.
list_remote_work filters: f">={s.remote_start}": begin(day 00:00), f"<{s.remote_start}": finish(day+1 00:00) — strictly remote_start-bounded to the target day.
ConflictError branch 'if not item.get(s.remote_end) or int(item["id"]) in overlapping_ids' — only reachable for records present in by_id, which excludes cross-day unfinished records.

test_manual_remote_duplicate_and_unfinished_interval: existing record with remote_end set to None must cause ConflictError with zero crm.item.add calls — but the tested record starts on the plan's own day, so the cross-day unfinished case is untested.

The SDK's own test double returns False for any filter when the field is None (unset never matches any operator), and plain string semantics also make '' fail a '>' bound — both encodings of an unset remote_end exclude the record from the overlap predicate.
repo A calls create_remote_work directly (no local overlap pre-check); show_day at :120 is the only other list_remote_work use and is read-only.

Independent verbatim harness output (sandboxed): case A unfinished previous-day 20:00 end=None -> in overlapping=False, in same_day=False, _find_duplicate=None, gate 'journal.reserve THEN crm.item.add EXECUTES'; A2 end='' identical; control B same-day unfinished -> ConflictError; control C finished cross-day overlap -> ConflictError; control D back-to-back ending exactly at plan start -> allowed.

conditions.description: The webhook owner has an existing remote-work record with remote_start strictly before the target plan day and remote_end unset (interval started in the UI or by a prior run and never finished). Given the daemon applies each new scheduled day, one stale interval causes one overlapping record per subsequent day until resolved.

Bitrix server-side crm.item.list filter semantics treat an unset/empty datetime field as not matching '>'/'<' range comparisons (standard SQL NULL-like semantics). Corroborated by the code's own dedicated same_day query and comment at service.py:352-353 (which would be redundant otherwise) and by the SDK's test double tests/fakes.py:58-59; the harness also shows the empty-string encoding behaves identically, so the finding holds for both representations of an unset field.

execution.attacker_perspective: No adversary is required: the webhook owner (or anyone using the portal UI on their behalf) starts a remote-work interval and never closes it; the automation daemon then applies the next day's schedule and the SDK's conflict scan does not see the open interval. From a control-defeat perspective, the documented overlap/unfinished conflict control (service.py:352-360, integration test) is bypassed by purely environmental data state.
instructions: Sandboxed harness copying the two conflict queries and the by_id loop verbatim from current service.py:322-361 plus list_remote_work filters :219-223; fake server applies the SDK's own fakes.py comparison semantics; no target package imported, no network. Run under sandbox-exec with env -i, ulimit -t 60 -f 2048 (agents/verify-03/artifacts/verify_overlap.out.txt).
execution.observed_result: A (end=None) and A2 (end=''): record in overlapping=False, in same_day=False, _find_duplicate returns None, _finish gate executes journal.reserve + crm.item.add -> an overlapping remote-work record is created although an unfinished interval from the previous day is open. Controls: B unfinished same-day 08:00 -> ConflictError('An overlapping remote work with different parameters already exists.'), write blocked; C finished yesterday 20:00->today 10:00 -> ConflictError, write blocked; D back-to-back ending exactly at plan start -> None, allowed (no false positive). Matches the hunter artifact h3_overlap_predicate.out.txt, re-derived from current source.

remediation.strategy: Extend the conflict set with a third query covering unfinished records whose start precedes the plan end, merging results into by_id before the existing loop; the loop's existing 'not item.get(remote_end)' branch then raises ConflictError for them. Cover both unset encodings server-side (empty-string equality filter and/or dropping the remote_end bound).

likelihood.reason: Triggered by a plausible operational data state, not an attacker: the owner leaves one remote-work interval unfinished past midnight (forgot to stop it in the UI) while the daemon schedules the next day. Once the stale interval exists, the bypass is deterministic and repeats for every subsequent scheduled day until manual cleanup; it requires no privileges beyond normal portal usage.

impact.reason: An explicit, tested integrity control (overlap/unfinished conflict, service.py:352-360) is fully defeated for this data state and wrong records are written to the production portal as the webhook owner, polluting time accounting and requiring manual deletion. Blast radius is honestly limited: one extra owner-scoped record per affected day, no privilege escalation, no data exposure, no cascading portal effects — a real boundary violation with limited blast radius, i.e. medium, not high.

confidence.reason: Predicate-level demonstration with code copied verbatim from the current source, reproduced for both unset-end encodings (None and empty string), with controls confirming the two queries and the loop behave exactly as designed everywhere else. Intent is proven by the code comment at service.py:352 and the SDK integration test at tests/integration/test_service.py:421-440; the sole environmental assumption (unset datetime fields never satisfy '>' range filters) is corroborated by the SDK's own test double and by the very existence of the same_day query. No alternative catching path exists: the xmlId exact-duplicate query cannot match a different-day or manual record, and repo A performs no additional scan.

title: Add-response id guard: str.isdigit() accepts Unicode digits int() rejects or reinterprets; ValueError escapes the SDK error hierarchy after the write and journal.reserve
description: In TimeManager._finish the response guard at service.py:437 evaluates `not str(item.get("id", "")).isdigit() or int(item["id"]) <= 0` inside a try (:433-438) whose except clauses (:439 BitrixAPIError, :444 asyncio.CancelledError, :447 TransportError) do not include ValueError. str.isdigit() accepts Unicode Numeric_Type=Digit characters that int() rejects ('①' U+2460, '²' U+00B2, '¹' U+00B9): isdigit() is True, then int() raises ValueError inside the guard expression itself, and that ValueError escapes _finish after crm.item.add already succeeded (:434) and after journal.reserve already wrote a 'pending' row (:427) — a known-outcome write left unrecorded until a rerun reconciles via the xmlId duplicate lookup (:414 -> :322-324, which precedes reserve) or reserve raises the designed UncertainWriteError. In the bitrix-auto-manage wrapper the raw ValueError additionally aborts the whole remaining window: runner.py:57/67/71 catch UncertainWriteError/NotFoundError/TimeManagerError only, and cli.py:145-149 catch TimeManagerError/KeyboardInterrupt only, so the process dies with an unhandled traceback. A second variant: non-ASCII decimal digits ('١' U+0661, '١٢٣', '٩', '۵') pass BOTH checks with int() reinterpreting the value (int('١')==1), so a wrong item_id is accepted, written to the journal with state 'succeeded' via _with_item (:391,:397) and journal.complete (:452-454), used to build item_url, and used for the verification read get_item at :456. Divergence verified byte-identical on Python 3.9.6 and 3.14.7 in a sandboxed stdlib harness (evidence: agents/verify-04/artifacts/guard_harness_py39_py314.out.txt); behavior is defined by Unicode character properties (append-only) and CPython's decimal-only int() parser, hence stable across 3.9-3.14.
root_cause: The guard predicate (str.isdigit, Unicode-aware, accepts Numeric_Type=Digit or Decimal) and the consumer coercion (int(), accepts only characters with decimal digit values) apply different Unicode acceptance rules, and the guard evaluates both in one short-circuit expression inside a try that catches only the SDK error hierarchy (BitrixAPIError, asyncio.CancelledError, TransportError — none is a superclass of ValueError, per errors.py where every SDK error derives from TimeManagerError(Exception)). Consequently the guard's own failure mode for isdigit-pass/int-fail inputs is an uncaught ValueError raised after the write and the 'pending' reservation, instead of the intended TransportError.
intended_behavior: Any add response whose item id is not a positive ASCII integer takes the TransportError path at :438, which the except at :447-449 translates into journal state 'uncertain' plus UncertainWriteError; the documented contract is that no portal echo produces an exception outside the SDK error hierarchy (errors.py: domain errors safe to display, secrets redacted, raw transport/parse exceptions suppressed).

trace.description: body = await self.client.call("crm.item.add", ...) — the HTTPS portal responder (semi-trusted, P4) fully controls body['result']['item']['id'], which flows unvalidated into the guard two lines later.

`if not isinstance(item, dict) or not str(item.get("id", "")).isdigit() or int(item["id"]) <= 0:` — for '①'/'²'/'¹' the isdigit() operand is True so int() is evaluated and raises ValueError inside the guard expression; for '١'/'١٢٣'/'٩'/'۵' both checks pass and int() reinterprets the value (e.g. 1, 123), so the mis-coerced id propagates.
journal.reserve(...) immediately precedes the try at :433 — a ValueError at :437 strands the row in 'pending' after the write already succeeded at :434.

Replay reconciliation confirmed: _find_duplicate is called BEFORE reserve (:427); its xmlId lookup at :322-324 filters by xmlId+assignedById, and on core match the duplicate branch :421-426 calls journal.complete, which flips the stranded 'pending' row to 'succeeded'. xmlId is deterministic, so a same-spec rerun always finds the crashed run's record; if portal-side fields changed, journal.reserve instead raises the designed UncertainWriteError for pending rows. Either way no duplicate write is possible.

trace.scope: TimeManager._finish except tuple (:439-449) and downstream consumers
trace.description: Except clauses cover only BitrixAPIError (:439), asyncio.CancelledError (:444), TransportError (:447); the ValueError raised at :437 is not caught, escaping _finish after journal.reserve wrote 'pending' and after crm.item.add succeeded. Downstream sinks of the wrong-id variant: _with_item int(item["id"]) and _url at :391/:397, journal.complete at :452-454 (state 'succeeded' with wrong item_id/item_url), verification read get_item(..., int(item["id"])) at :456; in the wrapper the ValueError escapes runner.py:57-75 and cli.py:145-149, aborting the remaining window with a raw traceback.

evidence.description: Exact current guard expression, re-read post-rewrite.

title: Unguarded int(parentId1208) coercion in _with_item after a delivered crm.item.add leaves the journal 'pending' and crashes the wrapper window; reconcilable only by rerun
description: Re-derived from current source and reproduced in a verbatim stdlib sandbox harness. In _finish, after crm.item.add succeeds, service.py:450 calls _with_item(plan, item, "created") OUTSIDE the except tuple at service.py:439-449 (BitrixAPIError / asyncio.CancelledError / TransportError only). _with_item (service.py:390-400) evaluates item.get("parentId1208") at :392 and int(parent_id) in the workday_id ternary at :398. If the server-echoed parentId1208 is a truthy non-int-coercible value, :398 raises ValueError ('T1208_42') or TypeError (dict/list) before journal.complete at :452-454, so a delivered, known-outcome write is journaled 'pending' (reserve at :427 precedes the try). ValueError/TypeError are not TimeManagerError subclasses: wrapper runner.py:57-75 catches only UncertainWriteError/NotFoundError/TimeManagerError, and wrapper cli.py:145-149 catches only TimeManagerError/KeyboardInterrupt, so the exception escapes as a raw traceback and the apply window aborts with remaining specs unprocessed. (The SDK's own CLI sanitizes this at cli.py:122, but the production entry for this repo is the wrapper daemon.) CORRECTION of the prior record CONFIRMED: reconciliation IS reachable — on rerun, _find_duplicate (:414) runs before reserve (:427); the xmlId lookup (:322-324) finds the created item (xmlId is part of the add fields, :92) and the duplicate branch (:421-425) calls journal.complete, whose ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET state='succeeded' (journal.py:84-88) flips pending→succeeded without hitting reserve's replay refusal (journal.py:71-72); reproduced in the harness. WHY needs_validation: the mechanics are fully confirmed, but the trigger requires the real portal's crm.item.add echo to carry a truthy non-int-coercible parentId1208, and that JSON type is not source-observable — _check_schema validates only the field's declared metadata type "crm_entity" (:123), client.call validates only the response envelope (client.py:81-97), the test fake echoes request fields verbatim (parentId1208 is sent as int, service.py:286), live tests are read-only (allow_writes=False) and never perform an add, and no doc or captured response records the echo shape. If a compliant portal always echoes int (plausible, given int-coercible LIST output), the crash path is unreachable and the candidate should be rejected; one owner-observed add response settles it.
claimed_root_cause: _with_item coerces the raw server-echoed parentId1208 with int() (service.py:398) at a call site (:450) placed after the successful crm.item.add and outside the write-failure except tuple (:439-449), so a non-integer echo raises ValueError/TypeError before journal.complete (:452), leaving a delivered write journaled 'pending' and crashing the wrapper window; no upstream layer (client envelope check, id guard at :437, _check_schema metadata check) constrains the echo's parentId1208 JSON type.

title: Work-activity journal created world-readable (0644/0755) and retained indefinitely beside a 0600 credential
description: OperationJournal._connection (journal.py:27-28) creates the state directory and SQLite journal with ambient-umask default modes (mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) + sqlite3.connect) and no chmod/fchmod exists anywhere in either repo, so under the common umask 022 the journal lands 0644 inside a 0755 directory. complete() persists the full OperationResult JSON (exact REST fields including free-text comments/descriptions, item URLs, timestamps). On the real host the journal is 0644 while the sibling credential .env is 0600, i.e. the derived work-data copy is strictly more exposed than the secret guarding the primary copy. There is no DELETE/VACUUM/compaction path in journal.py, so records are retained indefinitely; LIM-03/04/08 acknowledge plaintext storage and absence of deletion but no doc promises an owner-only file mode — the boundary evidence is the owner's own 0600 credential posture beside a default-created 0644 journal plus LIM-04's current-state claim that the embedding application protects its files. Impact is bounded by portal_url being stripped to scheme://netloc (config.py:87-90): the journal holds work-time records, comments, portal domain and user/item IDs, never the webhook token.
root_cause: Journal creation relies entirely on the process umask with no explicit permission control: journal.py:27-28 uses Path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) and sqlite3.connect(self.path, timeout=0), both honoring umask; grep across both repos finds zero chmod/umask/fchmod occurrences, so default deployments inherit distro umask 022 and produce a world-readable file in a world-traversable directory; Docker adds root ownership (no USER in Dockerfile) via the ./state:/app/state rw bind.
